info.title: API Reference
info.description: ProofAge is an identity verification and age estimation API. Use this API to create verification sessions, upload media (selfies and documents), and receive decisions via webhooks.

post.description:
Uploads a selfie or document image to the verification session.
Consent must be accepted before uploading. The file is validated
for quality (face detection, blur, brightness for selfies;
document detection, readability for documents).

Answers `200` with an empty body; a failed quality check answers `422`.

200.description: The media was stored. The body is empty.

422.description: The image failed a quality check; the code says which.

examples.message: Face validation failed. Please upload a clear, well-lit selfie with your face fully visible.

get.description:
Streams the bytes of a selfie or document image belonging to the
verification, served by ProofAge under the same API key and HMAC
signature as every other endpoint.

The response body is the image itself; `Content-Type` carries its MIME
type. Media that has been purged, has passed its retention window, or
does not belong to this verification answers 404.

200.description: The media file itself. Content-Type carries its MIME type.

404.description: Media does not belong to this verification, or is no longer available.

post.description: Creates a new verification session and returns a URL for the end-user to complete verification.

201.description: The verification session, with the url the person opens to complete it.

402.description: A live workspace has no payment method.

examples.message: A payment method is required to create verifications.

post.description:
Records the end-user's acceptance of the data processing consent.
Must be called before uploading media or submitting the verification.

200.description: Consent is recorded; media can now be uploaded.

get.description: Retrieves the current state of a verification session including its status and decision reason.

Retrieves sanitized age-threshold and gender estimates for age estimation workspaces.
The gender value uses 0 for female and 1 for male.

200.description: Verification age estimation result. Gender value mapping: 0 = female, 1 = male.

get.description:
Returns what was read from the identity document of the most relevant attempt,
normalised: dates as YYYY-MM-DD, countries as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (XK for Kosovo), and null for
anything the document did not yield or does not print. On identity (KYC)
workspaces `fields` carries eleven keys; on age verification workspaces only
`first_name`, `last_name`, `date_of_birth` and `document_number` are returned.
Each media item carries a `url` for the download endpoint, or null when the
media has been purged or has passed its retention window.

200.description: Verification document result. `type` and `gender` are open enums: handle values not listed here. `gender` is F, M or X, where X means the document states that the sex is unspecified. `other` in `type` is a readable document that is not an identity card, passport, driving licence or residence permit, such as a health insurance card. Countries are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (XK for Kosovo). A document that prints only the month or year of expiry reports the last day of that period; a partially printed birth or issue date is null. On a Mexican voter card or driving licence created before 20 August 2026 17:00 UTC, `gender` is null. The German identity card prints no sex, so `gender` is null there. A permanent document (for example `PERMANENTE` or `INDEFINIDA`) reads as a null `expiry_date`. `type` `id` is the same value the upload endpoint takes. `issuing_country` and `nationality` can differ, for example on a residence permit. `issuing_subdivision` is the state or province that issued the document, as a bare code beside `issuing_country` (for example `FL` with `US`), or null; today it is filled for US driving licences and ID cards. `place_of_birth` is the printed text, not normalised. `address` is the printed text as read, not parsed and not normalised, and may contain line breaks.

post.description:
Submits the verification for automated processing once the current attempt's media is uploaded.
An upload moves the verification to `started`. A facial age estimation that asked for a document
is submitted the same way, after the document is uploaded.

Answers `200` with an empty body; the decision arrives by webhook.

200.description: The verification was submitted. The body is empty.

422.description: The verification is not waiting to be submitted (`INVALID_STATUS`), or required media is missing (`MISSING_REQUIRED_MEDIA`).

error.message: All required media must be uploaded before submitting.

post.description:
Adds the face from this verification's selfie to your blocklist, shared by all your workspaces.
Later verifications with a matching face are declined.
Optional `reason` text is stored with the block and truncated to 1000 characters.

Optional `reason_code` classifies the block, and is what reporting counts: one of
`presentation_attack`, `fraudulent_document`, `scam_or_abuse`, `underage`, `other`.
Send it whenever a person made the decision — the admin consoles require it, so a
block that arrives without one cannot be told apart from an automated one.

get.description: Returns the workspace settings including flow type, verification mode, and age thresholds.
Returns the currently active consent version that must be presented to and accepted by the end-user.

200.description: The active consent version. Show the text at url, then send id and text_sha256 back when accepting.

apiKey.description: Your workspace public key (pk_test_… or pk_live_…).
apiKey.name: X-API-Key

hmacSignature.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the request, hex-encoded, keyed with the workspace secret key. See API authentication.
hmacSignature.name: X-HMAC-Signature

reason.description: Free text stored with the block; longer text is cut at 1000 characters.

BlockedFaceReasonCode.description: Why a person put this face on the blocklist. The admin consoles require one; the public API accepts it optionally, and propagated device matches carry none.
BlockedFaceReasonCode.title: BlockedFaceReasonCode

callback_url.description: Where the person's browser is sent after the final screen. Ignored unless the request is HMAC-signed.

external_id.description: Your identifier for the person. Ignored unless the request is HMAC-signed: the public key alone cannot tie a session to your user.

external_metadata.description: Free-form data returned in the API and webhooks. Accepted without a signature, so treat it as client-supplied.

metadata.description: Free-form data kept on the session and not returned to integrations.

type.description: What the file is: the person's selfie, or one side of their document.

side.description: Which side of the document. Required when `type` is `document`.

document.description: The kind of document. Required when `type` is `document`.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.

post.summary: Verification status changed, or document data corrected
post.description: ProofAge sends this request to the workspace's webhook URL each time a verification moves to `approved`, `declined`, `resubmission_requested`, `review`, `abandoned` or `expired`. One verification can therefore produce several events. The same request, with `event` set to `data.updated`, is also sent when someone on your team corrects the document fields the reader got wrong, from the console or the MCP server; `status` is then the verification's current status, unchanged. Dispatch on `event` first. Verify `X-HMAC-Signature` before trusting the body: it is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `{X-Timestamp}.{raw body}`, keyed with the workspace's active secret key. Respond with any 2xx. A 408, 429 or 5xx response, or no response within 30 seconds, is retried after 5, 15 and 60 minutes. See [Webhooks](/integration/webhooks).

parameters.name: X-HMAC-Signature
parameters.description: Hex HMAC-SHA256 of `{X-Timestamp}.{raw body}` with the workspace's active secret key.

parameters.name: X-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix time, in seconds, when the request was signed.

parameters.name: X-ProofAge-Webhook-Delivery-Id
parameters.description: ID of this delivery. A retry of the same delivery keeps it; use it to ignore duplicates.

verification_id.description: The verification this event is about.

event.description: What happened. `status.updated`: the verification moved to `status`. `data.updated`: someone on your team corrected document fields; `status` is the current status, which a correction never changes, `document` carries the corrected values and `changed_fields` names what changed. A payload without `event`, such as a retry of a delivery created before this field existed, means `status.updated`.

status.description: The status the verification moved to. On a `data.updated` event, the current status, unchanged.

external_id.description: Your identifier for the person, as sent when the verification was created.

external_metadata.description: The metadata you attached when creating the verification, returned as sent.

reason.description: The decision reason code when the status is `declined` or `resubmission_requested`; `null` otherwise. Also `null` on the `resubmission_requested` a facial age estimation sends when it asks the person for an ID (`GET` reports that verification as `documents_required`). When attempts run out, the `declined` event carries the last attempt's reason. See Decision reasons.

issuing_subdivision.description: The state or province that issued the document, as a bare code beside `issuing_country` (for example `FL` with `US`), or null. Today it is filled for US driving licences and ID cards. Present on every workspace and kept after erasure.

gender.description: `X` means the document states that the sex is unspecified.

nationality.description: Published only when the document itself states it.

address.description: KYC workspaces only. The printed text as read: not parsed, may contain line breaks.

document.description: The same object `GET /v1/verifications/{id}/document` returns, without `media` and `meta`, read from the attempt that decided the verification. Identity (KYC) workspaces receive eleven `fields`; age verification workspaces receive `first_name`, `last_name`, `date_of_birth` and `document_number` only, and the other seven keys are absent. `null` means the field was not read, is not printed on that document, or no document was read at all (a facial age estimation that passed without an ID, a test workspace, a wallet check); `document` itself is never null. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` and countries ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`XK` for Kosovo); `type` and `gender` are open enums. Fields your team corrected show the corrected value. A resend or a manual retry carries the document as it is now; an automatic retry carries the body as first sent. After the person's data is erased, only `type` and `issuing_country` are kept.

changed_fields.description: Only on `data.updated`: the names of what this correction changed, for example `["date_of_birth"]`. A name is a key of `document.fields`, or `type`, `issuing_country` or `issuing_subdivision`. Names only; the new values are in `document`.

duplicate_detected.description: Present and `true` only when the same face was found behind another verification in the workspace.

duplicate_count.description: Present with `duplicate_detected`: how many earlier verifications matched.

duplicate_of.description: Present with `duplicate_detected`: the first matching verification.

fingerprint_signals.description: Optional device and network signals collected during the session. Treat it as informational; its fields may change.

manual_moderation.description: Present when a person in the console approved or declined the verification by hand.

source.description: `tenant_admin` is someone on your team; `landlord_admin` is ProofAge staff.

source_status.description: On an approval: the status the verification had before it.

source_reason.description: On an approval: the reason code it had before it.
